data.raw_text:
Floods and droughts hit the Thailand, Mynamar, Vİetnam ad Philippinnes economy particularly hard

Climate-related damages as % of GDP 
Myanmar (MMR)
Myanmar stands out with the highest climate-related losses in the group. Damages are overwhelmingly driven by storms and floods, and the impact is amplified by a lower income base, making each shock disproportionately costly in GDP terms.

Thailand (THA)
Thailand ranks second, with losses close to 0.7% of GDP. The burden is dominated by floods and storms, while droughts add a smaller but persistent drag on agricultural output and rural incomes.

Viet Nam (VNM)
Damages are lower than in Thailand but remain substantial. Flooding is the primary driver, complemented by growing exposure to droughts and extreme temperatures, particularly in coastal and delta regions.

Philippines (PHL)
Overall losses are more moderate, yet storm-related damages are highly pronounced. Frequent but more fragmented shocks keep the GDP share below Myanmar and Thailand, despite very high event intensity.

*** Myanmar and Thailand clearly stand out. For Thailand in particular, climate risk has shifted from episodic disasters to a structural macroeconomic vulnerability, underscoring the need for sustained investment in flood control, urban resilience, and climate adaptation.

Source: @OECD

TRAFFIC ADVISORY

Delhi Traffic Police has made elaborate traffic arrangements in view of the Indian Navy Half Marathon to be held on 01.02.2026, promoting fitness and a healthy lifestyle. The event will be flagged off from Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium with around 15,000 participants.

Time: 04:45 AM – 09:00 AM

📍 PUBLIC ADVISORY
-Traffic will remain regulated on marathon routes during the above hours
-Commuters are advised to avoid affected roads as far as possible
-Use public transport to help reduce congestion
-Follow directions of traffic police personnel on duty
-Emergency vehicles will be facilitated uninterrupted movement
-Plan your journey in advance, especially if travelling towards Railway Stations/ISBT/Airports.

📍 Stay updated through Delhi Traffic Police official channels.

#DPTrafficAdvisory
